verdict.classifier1: The changed code is used in 31 other places that this PR does not edit.
verdict.reason: One extra unit test passes on the old code and fails on the new code. A named person must decide if that is OK.
notes: Severity went from Medium to High because that unit test fails.

reviewSummary: The fix is wider than the bug. It hides warnings in places that never crashed. The new unit tests do not prove the fix works.

findings.title: The fix hides more warnings than it needs to
findings.detail: The new check drops every warning that points outside this project. That stops the crash. But it also hides warnings in cases that never crashed. No unit test shows how many warnings are now hidden.

findings.title: A bad key on one kind of property is no longer reported
findings.detail: If a property has an empty key, the old code crashed. The new code says nothing at all. So the user gets no warning about the bad key.

findings.title: The new help page does not match the code
findings.detail: The help page for warning MsgPack004 says it only covers code in your own project. The code can still raise it for a parent type that comes from another project.

findings.title: The new unit tests do not prove the fix works
findings.detail: They only check that the output file exists and that there are no warnings. They do not check that the file can save and load the type from the bug report.

findings.title: One unit test locks in a missing warning
findings.detail: A member with no key now gives no warning in the project that uses it. The unit test treats that as correct. Its comment says the other project will report it, but no check shows that.

agent.context: bug report #2283 and the 4 files this PR changes

chat.q: Why did you hide the warnings and not fix only the crash?
chat.keys: approach filter warning crash chose design hide
chat.a: The crash came from a type that lives in another project. There is no line in this project to point a warning at. A checker is not allowed to point outside the project. So I made one check, `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation()`, that every warning goes through.

chat.q: What were you least sure about?
chat.a: Whether I hide too many warnings. Some types from other projects worked fine before. A few of their warnings are now hidden. I did not check that.
My unit tests check that the output file gets made. They do not check that it works. They also skip some kinds of types from other projects.

1.summary: Fixes a crash. The crash happened when your code used one kind of type from another project. The fix hides some warnings to stop the crash. It also hides some warnings that used to work.

sections.title: Why
sections.text: The tool crashed on one kind of type that comes from another project. The build still looked fine. But a file the app needs was never made, so some apps broke when they ran.

sections.title: Before → after
sections.text: Before: the tool crashed and the file was missing. After: no crash. But warnings about code in another project are now hidden.

sections.title: Must preserve
sections.text: Other types from another project already worked. They must still work, and still show their warnings.

sections.title: Approach
sections.text: All warnings now go through one new check, `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation()`. It drops any warning that points outside this project.

sections.title: Checks run
sections.text: Unit tests (`dotnet test`, a saved run on one machine, not the automatic server run): 170 of 170 pass. One extra unit test for `GetObjectInfo()` passes on the old code and fails on the new code.

sections.title: Open gaps
sections.text: The new unit tests only check that the file gets made. They do not check that it works. The new check also touches every warning, not just the crash.

sections.title: Rollback
sections.text: Undo the commit. Nothing else to clean up.
